This is the magic skill tree I have drawn:

The symbols: Since the movement of mana energy requires pathways either being neurons or wires, a mortal would use these specific symbols in their pathways in order to use mana. This makes magic use "semi-selective" because you cannot switch from one type of magic to another (too much), the pathways would need to change shape in order to do it.

Adjacent types: If one was to switch types of magic they would only be able to use the ones adjacent due to their similarity. So for example one could be good at Telekinesis and with enough skill and effort they could also start to be good at Psychokinesis. Higher-order mages/sentients can use more different types.

The Magic Types:

ENTROPY: The channeling of mana into direct energy, fastest way to get rid of it, most pure in energy conversion. Ex: Lightning bolt, shocks, energy beam.

THERMAL: Like entropy, thermal conducts the energy into plasma and heat. Ex: Fireballs, fire throwing, heating.

DESTRUCTION: Now using aspects of telekinesis, this is the use of energy and matter put together, in chaotic ways. Ex: Ice, Freezing, Water control, Shock waves.

TELEKINESIS: This is macro-telekinesis (like jedi throwing boulders). This is not precise or accurate, but it is powerful and can lift more than psychokinesis. Ex: Jedi force powers, throwing stuff.

PSYCHOKINESIS: This is micro-telekinesis, moving small things very precisely, its side effect is that it is "weaker" than telekinesis. Ex: Picking locks, crushing spines, force chokes.

RESTORATION: This is really just psychokinesis on a truely microscopic scale, repairing tissues and cells, putting wounds back together. It is actually very similar to necromancy when you think about it. Ex: Healing

NECROMANCY: This is macro-healing (ie very sloppy) combined with mass mind control. It doesn't make beings that can really live on their own anymore since it is a complete perversion of restoration, and requires constant control.

CONTROL: Control is mind-control on a macro level. Think "eye of sauron" where no orc's actions were specifically controlled but their motives were.

ILLUSION: A much weaker but more precise form of control, illusion is the bending of what minds perceive. This allows the user to become invisible, by making groups of people ignore their presence. It could also make them see a monster where there is not one, or see more clearly without a light. Ex: invisibility, illumination

TELEPATHY: This is the direct control of a person, in its complete most precise form. The amount of people someone could control is dependent on their skill level. Ex: Mind control, mind reading.

PSYCHOPATHY: (lol) This is the manipulation of emotions, much less intrusive than telepathy though more longer lasting. Ex: Calming, angering, inception powers.

ALTERATION: This is control of the mana winds. Its kind of out of place but I wasn't sure where to put it. This could either disperse mana winds, pushing them out of a location or concentrate them. Ex: In a battle, think support mages that channel mana to other mages.

Other notes:

Blessings of the followers of a god is something I will include in a later post, something like magic Orders.

Summoning wasn't included, I wasn't sure where to put it, or if it is actually a legitamite use of the magic as defined.

I'd move on to some criticisms about how the labels themselves are handled - for example, why is illusion different from telepathy different from psychopathy, when the most practical way to do illusion is to touch someone and 'telepathically' impose what they see onto them? Why are 'thermal' and 'entropy' different, when heat is actually the most entropic use of the energy, and all uses of the energy is inherently applied entropy - that being changing something with high potential energy, divine-ish mana, into something with lower energy (heat being the 'lowest' form of energy of all, since all other forms of energy eventually convert down to heat)? But that would imply that the logic behind the labeling in the first place is sound, and my previous post would question that.

I'm not trying to stifle your creativity or anything, or say 'Muh magic! You can't touch it!' I'm just encouraging you to think in terms of implications that might arise from the magic, rather than making labels without thinking too hard about it, because that makes for better world-building IMO.

To not be entirely critical without contributing, I'd think a more intuitive labeling for the world might be something like...

'Primal magic' - Direct force conversion, attempting to convert mana into things like fire, electricity, or light, with simple uses being to create a point of light in your hand, more complex uses being to create it more far away or to direct it and move this point around, have multiple points, putting more oomph into those points. Most can be done with basic circuitry already present in the nerve system, and so training would resemble martial arts, with specific forms.

'Internal circuitry' - Having a circuit of magic burned into the flesh to make specific configurations of nerves easy to achieve by basic flexing, at the expense of versatility. This is having fairly specific 'spells' that you can do much more reliably and without much martial skill of moving your body. However this can be combined with even more advanced martial techniques of body-motion, so you have complex circuits that you also manipulate, thereby having 'variables' in the spells that you can adjust. For example you might have circuitry for having a 'plane' of energy useful as a shield, and motion might determine what type of energy the shield tends to be made of, where it moves, and whether it's one large one or many small ones, and where the small ones are, f you are advanced - or you might have a simple, 5x5 foot 'kinetic shield' exactly 5 inches in front of your hand so long as you keep your body in a particular stance, if you just paid for the circuitry and didn't do much training.

'Simple extension' - A broad category of magic that includes people who don't really study magic as such gradually incorporating magical poses into their use of metal tools for increased effect. A knight that develops a sword style that makes very inefficient motions that would in our world be laughed at but in this one actually produce surprisingly strong blocks because of kinetic energies, or a thief that uses inefficiently shaped lockpicks and strange gestures to apply minor telekenesis to the insides of locks. Each one would require separate training, and many can presumably be enhanced with cooked-in circuitry.

'Linking' - Magic related to touching someone to affect them directly. Generally people are sort of 'magic immune' in that their circuits deflect the magic, and attempting to influence them anyways is probably a school of training in its own right. It's pretty excplusively touch ranged and may enable things from perception control to damage to (potentially) healing.

'Scalding' - The art of attacking someone with magic from a distance, by putting magic only where they explicitly have no circuits - mostly the outer surface of the skin - and gradually burrowing inwards. This would take a great deal of control over a very long distance and a very good understanding of where nerves are, so as to avoid them, and is very 'modular,' has a lot of variables, so migth be very impractical to try to make a device to do.

'Complex extension' - Making objects that extend the nerves, allowing for more complex circuits without having to internally scar oneself, or when the limits of internal circuitry have been reached - or for added flexibility. The art of making and using specially shaped impliments that aid in assorted effects. Weird wants and staves made with metal veins and designed to be held in specific ways, either useable by anyone with basic circuitry or only useful to someone with certain circuitry already in them.

I'm not sure you can really create 'darkness' or 'ice,' those are not energy, they are a lack of energy.
